newsitem.title: USA: Kodak says it is improving its cost structure.
newsitem.headline: Kodak says it is improving its cost structure.

text.p: Eastman Kodak Co Chairman George Fisher said the company continues to improve its cost structure.

Fisher made his comments in a released statement that accompanied Kodak's fourth-quarter earnings results on Thursday. The company reported earnings of $0.49 per share, including charges, compared with $0.80 per share in the year-earlier period.
Officials from the company were not immediately available.
Fisher pointed to the company's accomplishments in 1996 to illustrate ways in which the company has better positioned itself for growth.
The company has seen growth in emerging markets, including in China, Russia and Eastern Europe, Kodak said, although did not provide specific figures.

The company has also repositioned its Office Imaging business, introduced a corporate brand advertising program and completed a $1 billion stock buyback program, the company said. Kodak also launched a $2 billion buyback program.

The company also boosted its quarterly dividend to $0.44 per share from $0.40 per share -- a signal, said Fisher, that the company is confident it its "ability to continue to deliver improved results."
